behaviors.behavior: Local status at T1 always wins over a chronologically-later foreign status at T2>T1 for the same id
Local status wins an exact-timestamp tie against a foreign status (no tie to break)
Foreign status still fills a gap for an id with no local status event
A local decision living in the OUTBOX only (not yet tracked) still blocks a foreign override -- D1 union
A malformed local status event (invalid newStatus) does not block a legitimate foreign gap-fill
amend (local or foreign) stays purely chronological even when the id has a local status decision
A local+foreign amend exact-timestamp tie still resolves by file order (unaffected by the new rule)
Multiple foreign status events for a never-locally-decided id still resolve chronologically among themselves
A foreign append never seeds an item this tree never created (pre-existing guarantee, unaffected)
read_all_items composes the local reader and the cross-tree sibling reader end to end
A foreign status event with a non-string (unhashable) id does not crash the read -- external code review (glm) crash-guard finding
